findings.detail: Retains the actual database() main object, appends one byte to that exact owned held inode, and invokes unchanged immutable_query(). Its first operation is inputs.verify(), before any sqlite3.connect or query callback. The exact drift refusal and zero-connection predicate remain; re-entering auth_rows/database no longer causes the earlier absence guard to intercept this test.

All six payloads are hash/size checked and AST/compiled before imports. Only the same three already-reviewed import-safe libraries are loaded. The actual T5 guard precedes writes. The carrier appends only qa/mac_capture_sqlite_synthetic_r2.py and a new candidate receipt using create-only writes; it does not recreate ROOT/qa or execute capture/synthetic entrypoints.

All five full nine-field identities and byte/SHA pins exactly match the retained actual inert stdout blob cad3d4ecd0b33bcb3e21f9e9b4accb52cc2ed4de. The carrier checks named identity and complete held readback before and after the new source is written.

Commands outcomeUnknown includes command completion deadline, cleanup, stream closure and errors. Carrier and synthetic require final closure/anchor and the original 45-second deadline, followed by post-flush deadline and authoritative exit zero. Early candidate receipts cannot qualify.

limitations: This peer review used only Git and in-memory byte/diff/dispatch validation. It ran no host command, SQLite, child process or product fixture and does not grant runtime approval.
The supplied two selected-definition components and AST receipts were read as separate author evidence, not rerun or promoted to actual Mac seven-case qualification.
The previously noted public code-FD close failure reporting limitation remains: any such exception blocks complete/exit zero, but a failed report is not proof every public code descriptor closed.
Runtime binding is the observed Python/_sqlite3/source files and versions, not all dynamic libraries. No transactional/cross-agent snapshot or whole-database backup is claimed.
The B HA quiet window remains in force; all actual Mac dispatches remain root-coordinated.
